8.0.0.en: After Christ left the house of Simon the Pharisee, He began His second preaching tour in Galilee, in the early part of the second year of His ministry. He called people to repentance so that God might reign over their hearts, whether in the cities or the villages, caring for the rich and the poor, and His twelve disciples accompanied Him so that they might learn from His words and conduct and then preach in the same manner afterward when He commissioned them to do so; that is, it was an opportunity for them for spiritual discipleship.

8.1.0.en: Here Christ's care for women appears, for He allowed them to follow Him and hear His teaching, contrary to the custom of the Jews, which diminished their worth and did not give them an opportunity like that of a man; among the Gentiles also the status of woman was lower than that of man.

8.1.1.en: Among these women who loved Him because of their healing from diseases or evil spirits was Mary Magdalene (Magdala is a village on the Sea of Tiberias), who suffered from the domination of seven demons over her, and Christ cast them out of her and healed her, so she followed Him to the Cross and the burial, and was the first to visit His tomb at the dawn of the Resurrection, and He appeared to her, and she remained with the disciples and the believers until the end of her life.

8.1.2.en: As for Joanna, she seems to have been a rich woman who followed Christ until His burial, and carried spices to lay on His body. Some think that Chuza her husband was the king's officer whose son Christ healed, and so he and all his household followed Christ.

8.1.3.en: Then He mentions Susanna and others whose love was shown in providing money for the needs of Christ and His disciples. From this the humility of Christ appears, for He feeds the multitudes with five loaves, yet He needs food from the gifts of men, and is not troubled that some women spend on Him. This also shows Christ's concern for the service of women in the Church in what is suitable for them.

8.1.4.en: Accept with humility the love and service of others toward you, and even thank them for it, for this does not diminish your worth but adorns you with virtues.

8.2.0.en: Christ spoke in parables to bring the meaning near to the minds and hearts of the hearers, who were awaiting the Messiah as an earthly savior and material leader and not a Savior of their spirits; for this reason He used material parables so that through them they might understand His spiritual teachings.

8.3.0.en: This parable was explained earlier in (Mt 13:3-23; Mk 4:3-20), and one may refer to them. It appears in the parable that as the sower was moving toward the good ground, some of his seed fell by the way side, and the feet of people trampled it and the birds of the air ate the rest. Some other fell on ground full of stones with thin, shallow soil, and the seeds that sprang up found no moisture for their roots to absorb, so they withered away. Some seeds fell on ground full of thorns, and they sprang up with the good plants and choked them, shading them and absorbing the nourishment from the soil around their roots; but the seeds sown in the good ground produced perfect fruit, expressed as a hundredfold, because a hundred represents perfection. This parable is clear and easy to understand for whoever wants to hear the word of God.

8.4.0.en: Christ made clear the reason for His use of parables, which is that perhaps by this He may break into the hard hearts that hear Him and see and yet do not want to believe in Him and understand His words. But to the simple disciples who believe in Him, He explains the parable and offers direct spiritual teaching, that is, the mysteries of life with God, and how we give Him an opportunity to reign over hearts.

8.5.0.en: The interpretation of the parable is that God is the sower, and the seed is His word, which He wants to give to all even if He knows by His foreknowledge that they will refuse. So He offered the seed to the people who are like the way side, that is, those who do not open their hearts to receive His word, so the devil takes away the word and tramples it, and they gain nothing from it. The second class of people, represented by the rocky ground, receive the word but do not strive deeply to carry it out, so they leave God in the hour of temptation and fall back from Him to the world and its lusts. The third kind of people are those absorbed in their lusts, so even if they hear the word of God it does not affect them, because their lusts cover and choke the word. The last kind are the believers who understand the word of God and strive to carry it out with perseverance, and so they bring forth good fruit of spiritual virtues.

8.5.1.en: I wish you would regard the words of God that you read every day in the Holy Bible as a personal message to you from God, so that you respond to it and carry it out.

8.6.0.en: If a person wants to dispel the darkness of a place by lighting a lamp, it is unreasonable for him to cover it with a vessel that hides its light, or to put it under a bed so that its light does not appear; on the contrary, he puts it in a high place like a lampstand so that it gives light to the whole house or place.

8.6.1.en: What is meant by the light is the work of the word of God in us, so that the warmth of the Spirit within us appears in good works that draw many to love Christ. It is unreasonable to hide the light with a vessel placed over it, which is a symbol of the lusts of the world and the love of acquiring various material things that quench the warmth of the Spirit, or to put the light under the bed, which points to slackness, negligence and laziness; on the contrary, it is put in a high place, that is, we lift our lives above earthly things, so that we give light to all who are in the house, that is, the Church, and even to the whole world in which we live.

8.6.2.en: Consider what weakens you after you have been moved by the word of God or have made promises for the new life ... try to rid yourself of these hindrances and rise above them by giving them up.

8.7.0.en: This saying is also mentioned in (ch. 12:2; Mt 10:6). The "hid" thing is the word of God, which must be made known to all people; if you hide it by your sins, it will appear in the lives of others and reach you, but you will lose the grace of its being manifested in your own life. This saying is followed by the parable of the sower so that Christ may stress the necessity for those who believe in Him to apply His word in their lives, so that it appears spontaneously and affects those around them, and they do not hide His word as information inside them, but apply it and so receive the blessing of carrying it out, and others also are evangelized through them by His word.

8.7.1.en: Beware of hypocrisy, by which you hide some things within you and show the opposite, for the matter will be uncovered in spite of you with time and will appear for what it is, and you will be judged by God and men.

8.8.0.en: Christ stresses an important principle, namely that whoever is ready to obey God and strives in spiritual striving will be given more abundant blessings and his light will increase, so that he is satisfied and draws many to God. But whoever has no faith and spiritual striving, that is, does not apply the word of God in his life, the gifts of God to him, which in his pride he thinks are his own possession, will be taken from him and he will fall into doubts, because his knowledge is merely theoretical knowledge about God.

8.9.0.en: His mother is the Virgin Mary.

8.9.1.en: His brethren are the sons of His mother's sister, Mary the wife of Cleophas or Alphaeus. In Jewish custom the sons of an aunt are regarded as brothers.

8.9.2.en: These reached the place where Jesus was sitting, and could not enter to Him because of the crowd surrounding Him, so they stood outside.

8.10.0.en: Those around Him told Him that His mother and His brethren wanted to see Him, and this was a good intention on their part, and Christ rejoices in His relatives, and He cared for His mother even while on the Cross, but He wanted to raise everyone to the level of kinship with Him as His mother and brethren. How?

8.11.0.en: Christ declared that whoever hears His word and carries it out in his life has been raised to the level of kinship with Christ, and hearing alone is not enough but doing also.

8.11.1.en: It is to be noted here that after the parable of the sower, He stressed the importance of applying the word of God in the parable of the lamp, and then stressed it a second time when His mother and His brethren visited Him.

8.11.2.en: The humility of God calls you to be a brother to Him by keeping His commandments, for the word of God brings you near to Him so that you may enjoy fellowship with Him. So be diligent in reading the Holy Bible every day.

8.12.s.en: (5) The rebuking of the winds and the waves

8.12.0.en: Christ left the crowd and His relatives, and got into the ship with His disciples to cross from the western shore of the Sea of Tiberias to the eastern shore.

8.12.1.en: This is a symbol of Christ's bringing those who believe in Him across from darkness to light by means of His Cross or His Church, which is symbolized by the ship.

8.13.0.en: A storm of wind means violent winds, because the surface of the lake is 600 feet below the surface of the Mediterranean Sea, and the land surrounding it is high, so the air coming from beyond the hills around the lake is violent and stirs up the waters so that its waves rise.

8.13.1.en: It is mentioned here for the first time that Christ slept, to confirm His humanity. His sleep is a symbol of His rest in the hearts of His children and servants. The ship was exposed to violent winds that raised the waves, and they struck the ship and even the water entered it, and it was in danger of sinking, and consequently of the destruction of all who were in it.

8.13.2.en: The affliction may grow more intense while God is long-suffering, not out of neglect on His part or lack of feeling for you, but that in the end He may be glorified by a great miracle that shows His love for you.

8.14.0.en: The disciples used all their experience in steering ships and failed, and finally they had recourse to Christ in great agitation, declaring their helplessness and even their exposure to death. Then Christ arose and commanded the winds and the waves to be calm, and they obeyed at once, and this proves His divinity and His authority over nature.

8.14.1.en: The reason for the delay in solving the problem may be your not having recourse to God.

8.15.0.en: After Christ solved the problem, He reproved them for the weakness of their faith in Him and the delay of their recourse to Him, while to the disciples His authority and divinity became plainly evident, and they marvelled greatly at His power.

8.15.1.en: Help others first, then reprove them and guide them.

8.16.s.en: (6) The demoniac of the country of the Gadarenes

8.16.0.en: The country of the Gadarenes is one of the ten cities in Galilee, in which many Gentiles lived with the Jews; they are cities in the north of Judea at the Sea of Galilee, and this city is about 30 miles south-east of the Sea of Galilee.

8.17.0.en: St. Luke describes to us here the wretched state of a man in whom demons had dwelt for many years, so that they robbed him of his mind, stripped him of his clothes and drove him from living among people, so that he lived in the tombs. He is a symbol of mankind far from God, which has been stripped of the garments of righteousness and has lost its humanity and its love for people, and has even become dead while alive, since it dwells among the dead in the tombs; and this man left the tombs and came toward the city by the providence of God to meet Christ.

8.17.1.en: Consider what sin does to you, and how it makes you lose your loftiness as a human being and your love for those around you, and makes you like one dead in the sight of God, so that you may reject it by repentance and confession.

8.18.0.en: Despite the harshness and violence of the demons, they submitted in weakness and fear before Christ when this man worshipped Him, and the demons asked Christ not to torment them, since their rest is in tormenting human beings and their torment is the salvation of people from them.

8.19.0.en: Christ commanded the demons to come out of this tormented man whom they had deprived of living among people, and all human attempts to bind him, even with chains, had failed, for he would break them by the power of the demons within him and flee to the desert. For demons are not resisted by human thoughts and works but by prayer and the power of Christ.

8.20.0.en: Legion is the name of the largest division in the Roman army system, numbering from 3,000 to 6,000 soldiers.

8.20.1.en: St. Mark mentioned in his Gospel that the number of the demons in this man was two thousand, and the demons' answer to Christ means that they were a very great number.

8.21.0.en: The demons know that their end is eternal torment, and they also know Christ's authority over them, so they begged Him not to send them into the abyss, the place where the wicked wait until the Day of Judgment, when they will be cast into eternal torment.

8.22.0.en: There was a great herd of swine feeding in the mountains around the city, and this is contrary to the Jewish Law, which commands not to raise or eat swine, because they are a symbol of uncleanness and evil, since the swine wallows in dust and filth (in the New Testament, now that we have been taught the spiritual meaning, eating swine is no longer forbidden, but is ordinary food that God created for it). So the demons asked Christ to allow them to enter the swine, and they rushed down into the lake and were drowned, choked. Christ permitted this to declare His anger at disobedience to His law.

8.23.0.en: When the herdsmen saw their swine drowned, they were afraid and hurried to tell the people in the city of the Gadarenes and the surrounding area, and they all went out to see Christ, and found the one who had been mad and naked in the tombs clothed and seated, learning at His feet.

8.23.1.en: Thus grace restored his mind to the madman, and he settled in humility, loving spiritual discipleship in the teachings of Christ. And they were very afraid at the greatness of the miracle, because everyone knew the problem of this madman.

8.24.0.en: The people of the city heard from those who had seen the miracle its details, which showed the power and authority of Christ, and sadly they did not believe in Him but feared Him and asked Him to depart from their city, so He got into the ship and went away. Thus we find that fear deprives a person of enjoying fellowship with God: at the very time when the one who had been mad enjoyed fellowship with Christ by submitting at His feet, fear deprived the people of his city of this because of their unbelief.

8.25.0.en: Since the state of this wretched man had changed to joy after he came to know Christ, and he saw the ignorance of the people of his city in sending Christ away, he begged Him to let him follow Him so as to enjoy His fellowship. But Christ, contrary to His custom, told him to proclaim this miracle in his city. He did not fear, as in Judea, that they would make Him an earthly king over them, since this city was full of Gentiles, as we mentioned, so this was an opportunity for them to believe in God more than they believed in the power of the demons.

8.25.1.en: Be wise in speaking of God's work with you, so that it may be done with humility and concealment of yourself, and so you benefit others and are not fought with pride.

8.26.0.en: Jesus returned from the country of the Gadarenes to Capernaum, the city of Galilee in which He performed most of His miracles and gave His teachings, and found its people awaiting Him with longing.

8.27.0.en: The synagogue is the Jewish religious center in the city, in which the Holy Scriptures are read and preaching and teaching take place, and the ruler of the synagogue was a great religious rank. So it was a wonderful thing for Jairus to humble himself and hasten to Christ, falling down and beseeching Him to come and heal his daughter of twelve years who was dying, and this shows his humility and faith. But his faith was less than the faith of the centurion, who asked Christ to heal his servant by a word only from His mouth, whereas Jairus asked Christ to come to his house to heal his daughter. Jairus also is a symbol of the Jewish nation, to whose house Christ comes, that is, is born among it to save it, whereas the Gentiles, in the figure of the centurion, believe only in His word.

8.27.1.en: The twelve years signify the twelve tribes of Israel.

8.27.2.en: By faith you can obtain your needs from God your loving Father, who rejoices in your requests and wants to give you more than you ask or think, especially if your faith is joined with humility in the form of lowliness, tears, prostrations, fasts and continual prayers.

8.28.s.en: (8) The healing of the woman with the issue of blood

8.28.0.en: This woman was struck by an illness that made her bleed, and the doctors' attempts to treat her failed, and the illness lasted twelve years, a long time. She spent all her money and gained nothing. By this the weakness of human beings in healing themselves and their need of Christ appears.

8.29.0.en: The woman knew that she was unclean, according to the Jewish Law, because she had an issue of blood, so it was not fitting for her to touch Christ, but her faith and her need drove her to come secretly and touch the hem, that is, the edge of Christ's garment, to be healed, and she was healed immediately.

8.29.1.en: The garment of Christ is a symbol of His apostles and His Church, because of their clinging to Him, and the woman is a symbol of those who have received healing from their sins through their faith in Christ as a result of the preaching of the apostles and the Church.

8.30.0.en: Christ wanted to glorify this woman, so He said, Who touched me? The woman was afraid at first to declare herself, and everyone denied that they had tried to touch Him, while Peter and the disciples were astonished at His question, since they saw the crowds pressing on Him, so how could He say, Who touched me? But He made clear that it was not an ordinary touch but a miraculous touch, since power went out of Him to heal one in need.

8.30.1.en: Do not hasten to judge according to appearances, for God may have a wisdom that you will understand afterward. In every situation learn to pray that God may reveal to you His will that is hidden from your eyes, and to the measure of your humility and faith in prayer you will understand the wisdom of God.

8.31.0.en: When Christ announced that a miracle had occurred, the woman found no way but to declare what had happened to her, and she told her story before the crowds. And here Christ glorified her in three ways:

8.31.1.en: 1- He declared His fatherhood to her when He said, Daughter.

8.31.2.en: 2- He declared the greatness of her faith in touching His garment, since many touched Him and did not receive power because of their unbelief.

8.31.3.en: 3- He gave her inner peace, which is the greatest gift a person can receive.

8.31.4.en: To the extent that you hide yourself in humility, Christ glorifies you, and to the extent that you glorify yourself, you fall into pride and are deprived of His grace.

8.32.s.en: (9) The raising of the daughter of Jairus

8.32.0.en: Christ delayed on the way to proclaim the miracle of the healing of the woman with the issue of blood so that the faith of Jairus might be strengthened, and then the wars of the demons began with despair, for one came from his house announcing to him the death of his daughter, and Christ encouraged him, declaring that she was sick and would be healed, to confirm him in his faith. Christ said this because death is a sickness that has struck mankind, and Christ is able to heal it.

8.33.0.en: When Christ came to the house of Jairus, He went into the room of the dead daughter and took with Him His three close disciples, Peter, James and John, and also the girl's father and mother, so that they might see with their own eyes and understand and grasp the power of this miracle, so that their faith might increase and they might become witnesses of what they saw.

8.34.0.en: Christ tried to quiet the mourners in the house by saying to them that she was asleep, and they laughed Him to scorn because of their certainty that she was dead, and because they did not have faith like Jairus, his wife and the disciples. The weakness of your faith deprives you of understanding God's words and His work with you.

8.35.0.en: Christ took the girl by the hand and commanded her to arise, to show His divinity in a tangible way so that Jairus might understand it, and the girl arose immediately. And to confirm that her spirit had returned to her, Christ commanded that something be given her to eat, and she ate before them, and they were assured that she had returned to life.

8.36.0.en: The girl's parents were greatly astonished, while the faith of the disciples was stronger because of the miracles they had seen before and the teachings they had heard. And Christ commanded her parents not to spread the news of the miracle, because He does not want glory from men but wants the healing of souls by His teachings, and His miracles are to confirm His teachings so that they may believe in Him and be saved, and so that they would not be occupied with the material miracle and make Him an earthly king over them. For their idea of the awaited Messiah was mistaken, since they supposed Him to be an earthly king who would deliver them from the Romans and not eternal salvation.
